answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents anchor identity in cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. Rather than an identical mirror fleet, each registered node incurs an exponential capital exhaustion curve, scaling attacker cost as O(k^n). Validating unique hardware root keys through a rigid karst sinkhole registry, anchored with ferrous magnetic PUF fingerprints, renders massive swarms economically unviable.
